equivalentWithProof.rationale: Each later revision is compared with the exact record applyStepAdvance/applyStatusChange would build from the previous one. Those builders copy every immutable fact from the previous record, so a changed immutable fact makes the whole-record comparison fail; the IMMUTABLE check only provides an earlier, clearer message.
assumptions: Every revision after the first is either a single step change or a single status change, both compared with same(expected, rec).
evidence: applyStepAdvance and applyStatusChange start from { ...prev } and change only steps/status/revision/updatedAt/expectedHead/action.
Contract test: 'history chains' mutates treeSha, branch, manifest, identity and verification and each is refused.

equivalentWithProof.rationale: The expected record is built with updatedAt = max(prev.updatedAt, rec.updatedAt), so a revision whose updatedAt precedes the previous one differs from the expected record and fails the whole-record comparison.
assumptions: Chain steps are validated with the comparison against the rebuilt record.
evidence: applyStepAdvance and applyStatusChange set updatedAt to the later of prev.updatedAt and now.
Contract test: 'time moves backwards' case is refused.

evidence: #assertCanonicalAncestor runs before the first mkdir.
